decisions.statement: A caller hands over a page type.
A caller hands over a slug.
A caller hands over values.
A caller may hand over the path its page is written at.
Which values are committed is read from the page type rather than from the caller.
A property the page type declares as uncommitted is kept beside the page.
Every other property is written into the page.
The keys are written in the order the keys are declared.
The type deepest in the descent declares first.
A page the index already has is written back at the path the page has.
A page the index lacks and naming no path is placed under the folder its type is declared in.
A folder already named by the page type takes its pages under `pages`.
The folder a page type's pages sit in is answered here from that type alone.
A caller naming a page type that is no page is refused rather than guessed at.
A folder named by the page type's slug shorn of its opening is named by it.
A folder not named by the page type takes its pages under that type's slug.
A page whose type declares a property held beside the page takes a folder of its own.
A page with no such file yet takes that folder too.
A new page whose folder holds its pages in folders takes a folder of its own.
A page whose type asks for a folder takes one whatever that folder holds.
A page the index already has is left where that page sits.
A property the root `page` type declares is no reason for a folder of its own.
That folder is the page's slug with the name above the folder taken off the front.
Which properties are held in a file is read from the index.
A value under a key the page type declares no property for is refused.
A value under a property the page type declares secret is refused.
A page has the page type the caller named.
A page names the file its type is written at where the page type states one.
A page states the page type the caller named under `type`.
That key is stated here rather than kept from the page.
A page has the slug the caller named.
A slug past the hundred characters a page's slug holds is refused.
That slug is refused before the page type it names is looked for.
A slug past that length is refused rather than shortened.
A slug making a name no `export const` may be declared under is refused.
A page the index already has keeps the identity the page has.
A caller may write its values over the values the page already has.
A key the caller does not name is kept from the page rather than dropped.
A caller stating `merge` composes its body from the value the page already holds.
A body composed that way holds whatever moved under it since that value was read.
`merge` is what marks a caller that reads a body and writes that body again.
A value held in a file beside the page is kept as the extension the page states.
A value under a file property names that file's ending rather than that file's body.
A caller may hand over the body a file property holds beside its ending.
That body is put at the file the ending names.
A body handed over for a key held in no file beside the page is refused.
A body handed over for a file named rather than placed beside the page is refused.
A body handed over where nothing names the file's ending is refused.
A value under an entry property is the rows themselves or that file's ending.
The files those rows fill are put alongside the page with those rows.
A numbered file those rows no longer fill is taken away.
A page naming no ending for its entries takes `jsonl`.
A value that cannot name a file's ending is refused.
A merge into a page the index does not hold composes that page as a new page.
A caller states no identity for a page being created.
Several pages compose into the files a single write puts and keeps and takes away.
The page types a composing reads are read once for every page it composes.
A caller composing page by page may hand that reading in rather than paying it.
A caller handing none is answered from a reading made for that one page.
One page refused refuses the whole list.
Nothing here writes a file.
A body composed for a page already there is that page's whole body written again.
The id the page already holds is carried into a body composed without `merge`.
Nothing here answers the body text a page held when the new body was composed.
A caller holds the body a page held when that caller's new body was composed.

definition: the values a caller hands over, made into a page and what it keeps beside it
